_note: v7 (zero-shot, BioCLIP backbone): v3 with ONLY the backbone changed, OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 -> BioCLIP (imageomics/bioclip, also ViT-B/16, CLIP fine-tuned on TreeOfLife-10M biology images). Question: does biology-specific pretraining know crops and plant diseases better before any training? Same prompts, names and descriptions as v3 (HM 10.2%), so the difference is the backbone alone. Pairs with v8 (BioCLIP + v6 training recipe).
_result: BioCLIP is much worse than OpenAI CLIP zero-shot: harmonic mean 3.3% (v3, same prompts on OpenAI CLIP: 10.2%), top-5 HM 7.6% (v3 30.0%); seen top-1 3.1%, unseen top-1 3.5%. Even the crop is right only 23% of the time on test_seen (v3 43%) and disease 4.5% (v3 15%); the unseen-only diagnostic is 13.5% (v3 48.5%), barely above the 10% chance level. Likely cause: BioCLIP's text encoder was trained mostly on taxonomic captions (Latin names and taxonomic ranks), so common-name sentences with long symptom descriptions are far from its training text; biology-specific pretraining does not help zero-shot here. Whether its image features help once the prompt vectors are trained is tested in v8.

model._note: BioCLIP via open_clip's hf-hub loader (pretrained null). Same architecture as v1-v6 (ViT-B/16 image encoder, 77-token CLIP text encoder, argmax pooling, 512-d), so prompts and code are unchanged. Its preprocessing is the same resize 224 / centre crop / CLIP mean-std.
